## Study Populations
Two datasets were used in this PhD (Study II and study III) which are presented below
### CANCAN
The CANCAN data was collected in an observational case-control study from three hospital outpatient clinics in Denmark, Jutland.
The aim of the CANCAN Study was to investigate if cardiac autonomic neuropathy (CAN) assessments, CGM and heart failure indicators can be used in risk stratification in people with T2D. Participants were included if they were adults (< 18 years old), had T2D for at least a year, and excluded if they had atrial fibrillation or laser-treated eye disease within the past 3 months, were pregnant or lactating women, had a life-threatening disease with an expected survival of under a year, or were unable to understand and give their consent due to cognitive disabilities. Data were collected during a clinical examination, during which blood and urine samples were obtained, and a blinded CGM sensor was inserted. Blood samples to obtain NT-proBNP values were collected when the CGM sensors were returned, after the 2-week CGM data collection period had ended.

### T1DX
The T1DX racial differences dataset was collected by the T1D Exchange, a nonprofit organization, from diabetes centers in the United States (JAEB). The study focused on determining whether a racial difference exists in mean blood glucose and HbA1c levels between non-Hispanic Black and non-Hispanic White people with T1D. The study defined race and ethnicity through self-identified and self-reported ethnicity/race verification forms (Bergenstahl 2017). Further information on the definition of Hispanic, non-Hispanic, Black and White can be found in Bergenstahl et al.(Bergenstahl 2017). We, the authors, acknowledge that race and ethnicity are complex and not easily defined constructs, however we will use the word race moving forward since it aligns with the protocol and studies on the collection and analysis of the T1DX dataset (Kaneshiro2011, JAEB, Bergenstahl et al.,  2017). Participants were grouped by age within each race. Between 8 and 17 years old and from 18 years and older. A blinded modified investigational version of Abbott Laboratories Diabetes Care’s Flash Glucose Monitoring System (CGM) was used for 12 weeks. The study was conducted in accordance with the principles of the Declaration of Helsinki and approved by the relevant institutional review boards. All participants provided written informed consent, with assent obtained where applicable (Bergenstahl 2017).
